The denominator is $1+2\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1-2\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1-2\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5-2\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}} & =\frac{5-2\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1-2\text{i}}{1-2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{5-10\text{i}-2\text{i}+4{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{2}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5-12\text{i}+4(-1)}{1-4(-1)} \\  & =\frac{5-12\text{i}-4}{1+4} \\  & =\frac{1-12\text{i}}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\frac{1-12\text{i}}{5}=\frac{1}{5}-\frac{12}{5}\text{i}
$$
